title: Stochastic Preflight: Monte Carlo Release Sampler for LTS Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a stochastic preflight harness that can sample realistic upgrade scenarios across LTS channels and flag regressions or brittle behavior before rollouts. Rather than a deterministic smoke battery, this job runs thousands of lightweight stochastic trials (Monte Carlo sampling) combining traffic shapes, model variant fallbacks, kernel scheduling differences, network hiccups, and KV cache cold/warm starts to surface flakey regressions and SLO violation modes that single-run smoke tests miss.

Scope: prototypes for hosted and dedicated stacks, focused on the runtime and routing layers. The harness will: 1) synthesize traffic traces with configurable distributions (seq len, request interarrival, token per request); 2) randomly vary model variants and quantization profiles within compatibility bounds; 3) inject region failovers and simulated quota throttles; 4) run a small eval set for quality regressions on sampled traffic; 5) produce aggregated risk scores and per-signal fingerprints for use in rollout gates.

Why this is different: existing preflight suites run deterministic smoke and perf benches. This task intentionally trades deterministic coverage for probabilistic discovery: it prioritizes finding low-probability-but-high-impact regressions (e.g., rare KV cache invalidation + cold-start + burst). The output is a probabilistic risk estimate and a set of reproducible seeds that can be replayed for root-cause.

Implementation notes: harness implemented as a standalone job in the release-validation repo, parameterized by a scenario DSL. Runs will be parallelized across the CI fleet using our runner pool. We will integrate with the Console to emit a Monte Carlo risk dashboard (histograms, tail-percentile heatmaps, seed replay links) and wire a gating policy: if risk_score > threshold OR p99 latency delta > 15% OR eval-quality drop (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity on small prompt set) > 3% then fail preflight.

Trade-offs and constraints: stochastic sampling increases non-determinism in CI — all runs must publish seeds and a deterministic replay mode. Large sample sizes are expensive; we will bootstrap with 1k trials of fast micro-scenarios and iterate once signal quality is validated. Initial rollout scope excludes on-prem private package due to environment variability, but will produce environment-agnostic seeds that on-prem infra owners can replay locally.

Artifacts: Confluence design doc (CONFLUENCE:RELEASE/SAMPLER-2026), prototype GitHub PR (github.com/redwood-inference/release-validation/pull/1423), initial console mockups (drive.redwood/MC-risk-panel-v1).
steps: Define scenario DSL covering traffic distributions, model variant selection, quantization profiles, region failover events, and KV cache states
Implement sampler engine and seed serialization in release-validation repo
Create lightweight microbench harness for parallel execution (1k trials target for initial run)
Wire evaluator: 50-shot prompt set covering hallucination, completion correctness, and format stability
Integrate with Console: risk dashboard and seed replay endpoints
Add gating policy to preflight pipeline with adjustable thresholds and automatic PR annotation
Run pilot on runtime-1.22 branch and iterate on signals and thresholds
acceptance_criteria: Sampler can execute 1,000 micro-scenarios in under 6 hours on CI fleet and produce a consolidated risk report
Each failed run includes 3 reproducible seeds that trigger the failure when replayed deterministically
Console displays a Monte Carlo risk histogram, top contributing signals, and links to replay logs
Gating policy triggers on composite risk or any single signal breach and annotates the release PR with findings
False positive rate for the pilot is <= 10% when validated against known-good baseline runs
